# DESIGN.md — Coffee to Grow

archetype: garden-daylight
rationale: Coffee to Grow serves only by day (menu daily 8:40 am to 4:29 pm), prices everything between $1.50 and $6.99, and has one photograph and no written story, so garden-daylight lets the brand's own greens and cream carry a light, plain-spoken page that puts serving times, prices and the churro lattes up front, with a pale sage ground in place of the cream-and-serif look because the brand font is Inter.
interaction_level: L1

personality: [unhurried, sunlit, plain-spoken, neighbourly]

typography:
  display: "Inter"
  body: "Inter"
  accent: none
  scale: 1.25
  notes: Inter is the brand's heading and body font, so the personality comes from how it is set. Display runs at weight 600 with tracking of -0.03em and line-height 1.02, in sentence case, never all-caps. The hero headline and the two churro names break the scale and go much larger (clamp 2.75rem to 7rem). Below them the scale steps down 1.25 at a time to a 1.0625rem body at 1.65 leading. Category and section labels are 0.875rem, weight 600, sentence case, in the primary colour with a hairline beneath, not letter-spaced caps. Prices use tabular-nums at weight 500 so the columns line up.

palette:
  primary: "#273728"
  secondary: "#041F2C"
  accent: "#F8F3E7"
  ground: "#F4F6EE"
  surface: "#E7ECDD"
  ink: "#142016"
  muted: "#4D5E52"
  border: "#C9D2BD"
  application: Primary (deep green) carries the hero panel, the churro band, links, category headings and rules. Secondary (deep navy) carries the closing contact band and the footer, so the page ends in a different dark from the one it opens with. Accent cream is only ever type, rules or button fills on primary or secondary surfaces, never text on the light ground, where it would vanish. The page ground is a sage-leaning daylight paper with a sage surface one step from it, and the dark bands stay as bands so the page as a whole reads as daytime. Ink is the primary pushed down toward black, muted is a green-grey that stays above 4.5:1 on both ground and surface, and the border is a sage-grey hairline. These neutrals are tinted from this brand's green, so they would not sit right under any other brand.

composition:
  whitespace: balanced
  photography: supporting
  card_usage: none
  mobile: The hero stacks, with the photograph on top at 4:3 and the green panel full-width beneath it with no overlap. Headlines drop to about 2.25rem, and the two churro names to 2.75rem with the stagger removed. Menu rows go to one column. The category jump-row on /menu becomes a horizontally scrolling text row that sticks under the header. The phone number is always a full-width tap target. No sticky bar and no floating action.

pages:
  - path: /menu
    title: Coffee, Tea & Pastry Menu with Prices | Coffee to Grow
    description: Full menu and prices at Coffee to Grow in Front Royal, VA: espresso, churro lattes, pour overs, cold brew, tea, hot cocoa, waffles and homemade pastries.
    h1: Menu
    intent: What can I get here and what does it cost?
    nav: header
    takes: [offerings]
    sections:
      - id: menu-intro
        intent: Tell the visitor straight away that everything is served all day, within the daily window, and let them jump to what they want.
        spec: Left-aligned on the ground, no image. The h1 "Menu" is set at 4rem in the display weight. Beneath it is one line, "Everything below is served daily, 8:40 am to 4:29 pm." Beneath that is a row of the ten category names as plain text links to anchors on the list, separated by hairline dividers. They are Espresso, Pour Over Coffee, Cold Brew, Hot Chocolate, Italian soda, Homemade Pastries, Soda and Juice, Tea, Breakfast and Blended Drinks. On mobile the row scrolls horizontally and sticks beneath the header.
      - id: full-list
        intent: Carry every one of the 29 items and every price, easy to scan on a phone.
        spec: CSS columns, two on desktop and one on mobile, with `break-inside: avoid` on each category so no group splits. Each category has a sentence-case semibold heading in primary with a hairline rule beneath it and 3rem of air above. Item name sits left and price right on one baseline with a dotted leader between them. The description, where one exists, sits under the name in muted at 0.9375rem. Prices and ranges are written exactly as given, such as "$3.99 - $4.99". Omit a description that only repeats the item's name (Crafted Cold Brew). Keep "per person" on the Pour Over Coffee description. No images, no cards, no borders around rows. Show no stock flags such as "out of stock", "low stock" or "sale", and no add-to-cart controls.
      - id: menu-close
        intent: End the page on how to get the order, by phone or by walking in.
        spec: Full-width band in secondary with cream type. On the left, "Questions about the menu? Call" with (540) 325-0026 set as display type at 3rem as a tel link. On the right, the address exactly as written, 916 John Marshall Hwy, Front Royal, VA 22630, USA, with the line "Menu served daily, 8:40 am to 4:29 pm" beneath. No form, no ordering buttons, no email. On mobile the two columns stack with the phone first.

composition:
  Nobody plans a trip for this café's story, and the owner has not written one. People choose it because it is on John Marshall Hwy, the drinks cost between $1.50 and $6.99, and the menu runs daily from 8:40 am to 4:29 pm. So the first screen carries the address, the serving window and the churro lattes, pour overs and pastries, and offers one step, the menu. The business's own headline leads with the churro latte and its waffle shares the cinnamon recipe, so that pair gets the page's only moment of scale. A deliberate seven-item sample shows the range of prices and sends the rest to /menu. FAQ and contact are short and sit at the end, and the header's single action is the phone number, the same action the page closes on. The page holds back a story, reviews and a gallery because none exist, and does not pad.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: Say in three seconds that this is a café on John Marshall Hwy in Front Royal serving churro lattes, pour overs and homemade pastries by day, and offer the menu as the single next step.
    spec: >
      Editorial-split. The right 60% is the one supplied photograph (hero.backgroundImage), cropped with object-fit cover and bleeding to the top and right edges. It is shown as it is, with no overlay or filter, so the page stays in daylight. The left 40% is a primary-green panel that overlaps the photograph by about 3rem at the seam. In the panel, a small cream line reads "Front Royal, VA". Below it is the headline from hero.title ("Churro lattes, pour overs and homemade pastries on John Marshall Hwy.") at clamp 2.5rem to 4.5rem, in cream, weight 600, tracking -0.03em. The standfirst is hero.subtitle at 1.0625rem in cream. Beneath that, one small line: the address 916 John Marshall Hwy, Front Royal, VA 22630, USA, then "Menu served daily, 8:40 am to 4:29 pm". One button only, "See the menu" linking to /menu, filled cream with primary text. On mobile the photograph sits on top at 4:3 and the panel runs full-width beneath it with no overlap.
  - id: offerings
    priority: essential
    show: "7 of 29, chosen for range, links to /menu — Churro latte, Churro Waffle, Espresso shot, Pour Over Coffee, Gourmet Hot Cocoa, Chocolate Chip Cookie, Soda"
    intent: Make the churro pair the thing people remember, show the price range from $1.50 to $6.99 across coffee, cocoa, waffles and pastry, and send the rest to the full menu.
    spec: >
      Two-tier. The top tier is a full-width primary band with cream type, holding the distinctive moment. "Churro latte" and "Churro Waffle" are set as two stacked display lines at clamp 2.75rem to 7rem, weight 600, tight tracking. The second line is indented by about two columns on desktop. Each name has its price at 1.5rem in tabular figures on the same baseline, on the right ($5.99 - $6.99, and $4.99). The waffle carries a one-line description in fresh words along the lines of a cinnamon-led recipe, topped how you like. The latte carries no description, because the content has none. The lower tier sits on the ground. On the left, at a narrow measure of about 34rem, are five rows: Espresso shot $2.99, Pour Over Coffee $5.25, Gourmet Hot Cocoa $6.99, Chocolate Chip Cookie $3.99 and Soda $1.50. Each has the name left and price right on one baseline with a dotted leader, and no images, cards or borders. On the right is an oversized "$1.50 - $6.99" at about 5rem in primary, with a muted caption, "the spread across 29 items in 10 groups". A text link, "See all 29 items", leads to /menu. On mobile the indent goes, the numbers stack above the rows, and the link becomes a full-width tap target.
  - id: faq
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: Answer the four practical questions that people search for (where, when, what and how to reach us), quietly and in the café's own facts.
    spec: >
      Full-width band on the surface colour. A two-column split on desktop: a short sentence-case heading, "Good to know", at 2rem on the left, and on the right the four questions stacked as inline-list. Each question is a 1.125rem semibold line with its answer beneath in body size, and a hairline separates the pairs. No accordion, no icons, no cards. Use the answers as given in the content, with the same address, phone number and "8:40 am to 4:29 pm" window. On mobile the heading sits above the stacked list.
  - id: contact
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: Close on the one action, call or come in, with the address and the serving window impossible to miss.
    spec: >
      Full-width band in secondary with cream type, set as a call-first block. On the left, the phone number (540) 325-0026 at 4rem as a tel link, with a small line above it, "Call us". On the right, the address exactly as written, 916 John Marshall Hwy, Front Royal, VA 22630, USA, as a link to a maps search for that exact address. Beneath it, "Menu served daily, 8:40 am to 4:29 pm". No email, no map embed, no form and no social icons, because none of those exist in the content. On mobile the phone comes first, full-width, then the address and the times.

avoid:
  - A serif display face or a cream-ground-with-big-serif look. The brand is Inter throughout, and the personality comes from weight, tracking and scale.
  - Dark, moody evening-bar styling. This is a daytime café, so keep the ground light and use the primary and secondary greens in bands, not as the whole page.
  - Leaf, sprout or plant clip-art or icons to illustrate the name "Coffee to Grow". It is the most generic reading of the name, and the page has no photography of plants to back it.
  - Stock coffee-bean, latte-art or avocado-toast imagery. The only photograph is the supplied one, and nothing else is added.
  - Order online, Pickup, Delivery, Shipping, cart or checkout controls, and the "out of stock", "low stock" and "sale" flags carried over from the old Square storefront. None of these are in the content.
  - A card grid of menu categories, a photograph per item (none exist), or a "Fresh · Local · Handmade" icon row.
  - An invented story, reviews, opening-hours table by weekday, email address or social links. The only times on the site are "daily, 8:40 am to 4:29 pm", worded as when the menu is served.
  - Cream accent used as text or lines on the light ground, where it disappears. It appears only on primary and secondary surfaces.
  - Hiding the serving window. It must appear in the hero, the FAQ, the contact band and the menu page.
